taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Regional Texas treatments may use Passiflora lutea var. glabriflora; the learner remains species-level.

evidence: Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center's Purola Preserve natural flora lists Passiflora lutea among plants occurring naturally and not introduced.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Passifloraceae herbarium index includes Passiflora lutea.
Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a field-based treatment of Passiflora lutea var. glabriflora within the local flora.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Cultivated vines and garden escapes are not used as native-county evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the petiole and leaf shape. Yellow passionflower has no petiole nectar glands, and its small 3-lobed leaves are usually wider than long with broad rounded/obtuse lobes and entire margins. Then confirm the very small greenish-yellow flower and small purple-black berry.
diagnostic_traits: perennial climbing or trailing vine with axillary tendrils
petioles eglandular — no paired extrafloral nectary bumps
leaf blades shallowly to moderately 3-lobed, usually wider than long
lobes broad and rounded to obtuse; margins entire rather than serrate
fine veins prominently raised on the lower leaf surface
flowers small and inconspicuous, roughly 2–2.5 cm across in regional material
sepals green; petals pale green-yellow; corona pale green/white to yellow
ripe berries small, purple-black, roughly 8–15 mm

confusers.separator: P. tenuiloba has petiole glands and very narrow, deeply divided 3–9-lobed 'birdwing' leaves; P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves.

P. incarnata has two conspicuous petiole glands, deeply 3-lobed serrate leaves, much larger flowers, and large maypop fruits. P. lutea has glandless petioles, entire leaf margins and tiny flowers/fruits.

diagnostic_roles: leaf face showing broad rounded three lobes
petiole macro demonstrating absence of nectar glands
direct P. tenuiloba and P. incarnata petiole/leaf comparison
photo_verification.provenance_note: The highest-value learner image is a petiole/leaf close-up proving the absence of paired nectar glands.
